item.title: Notesy 3.0.0
item.description:
Notesy v3.0.0
Highlights • Self-updating — Check for Updates now installs the new version for you. It downloads the release, verifies it, replaces Notesy.app and relaunches, no dragging files around. • Still manual, still private — nothing checks for updates on launch or in the background. It runs when you pick Check for Updates from the app menu or press the button in Settings. • Verified updates — every release is signed with an EdDSA key, and the replacement app's own code signature is checked before it is swapped in. A tampered download is rejected. • Same Settings and menu — Check for Updates lives in the app menu and in Settings › Updates.
Everything from 2.6.0 is still here: drawing notes, sketching over text, textured paper, and the check that told you when a new version existed.
Requires macOS 14 or later. Unzip and move Notesy.app to Applications.
Added
Writing• Word count / reading time — shown right-aligned in the title band while a text note is selected ("127 words · 1 min read"). Updated live as you type.• Export / print — File → Export as Markdown…, Export as PDF…, Print… (⌘E, ⌘⇧E, ⌘P). Markdown strips only newlines; PDF prints the page with a heading + body, and for drawings prints the rendered ink.• Focus mode — View → Focus Mode (⌘F) hides sidebar, list and toolbar, leaving just the page. Activates again to restore them.• Pin/Unpin Note — Edit → Pin/Unpin Note (⌘⇧P) or right-click a row → Pin Note. Pinned notes float to the top of every list view; a small pin icon marks them in the row.Drawing• Per-tool colour memory — pen and highlighter keep their own last colour across switches, notes and relaunches (persisted in UserDefaults). Switching to a tool that had a saved colour restores it immediately.• Stroke commits save ink immediately — writing the sidecar file after each committed stroke means a crash or quit now loses at most an ongoing gesture instead of the whole session.Organisation• Trash with restore — deleting moves a note into the Trash folder (shows a count badge on the Trash row). Right-click a trash row → Restore Note, or select Trash → click Empty Trash… to delete forever.• Quick Switcher (⌘K) — opens a 520×420 search panel over the canvas. Type a title or body fragment, see filtered matches live, press Return to jump to that note, Escape to close. Also reachable from View → Quick Switcher….• Right-click context menu on list rows — Pin Note, Share Note…, Move to Trash (or Delete Forever / Restore Note when in Trash). No need to reach for toolbar buttons anymore.

item.title: Notesy 2.6.0
item.description:
Notesy 2.6.0
Check for updates, sketch on top of your notes, and put the page on real paper.
Highlights • Check for Updates — the Notesy menu now asks GitHub for the newest release and tells you whether you're current, with a Download button straight to the release page. It only runs when you ask; nothing phones home on launch. • Sketch on this note — draw directly over a text note. Ink sits on the visible page while the title band stays editable, so a margin doodle, a circled paragraph or a signature lives with the note it belongs to. • Sketch ink is part of the note — it's saved alongside the text, survives relaunch, and you can switch a note between text, sketch over text, and a full drawing note without losing the ink. • Textured paper — a new Settings › Paper switch lays the page on a photo of real paper, for typing and drawing alike. It's multiplied over the theme's own page colour, so dark themes keep dark paper and light text stays readable. Applies to drawing notes, sketch overlays and note thumbnails. • Drawing fixes — the ink surface now starts below the title band instead of under it, and the drawing palette is split into two fitted rows that scale down and stay inside the editor at every window width.
Everything from 2.5.0 is still here: the three-column glass workspace, the spatial canvas, and the nine themes.
Requires macOS 14 or later. Unzip and move Notesy.app to Applications.
